description: Page-Aligned Data Loading with Shuffle Buffer - Iterate by Parquet pages with shuffle buffer for ~1x I/O amplification under memory pressure

userStories.title: Page-aligned IterableDataset core implementation
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a page-aligned IterableDataset that iterates over Parquet pages and yields individual samples through a shuffle buffer, so that I/O amplification is minimized while samples are randomly ordered.
acceptanceCriteria: New class LiberoYoumuPageAlignedDataset(IterableDataset) in submodules/youmu/python/youmu/libero_dataset.py
Constructor accepts same args as LiberoYoumuDataset plus shuffle_buffer_size (default 10000) and page_cache_size (default 3)
On __iter__: generates shuffled (file, row_group, page) triples via get_shuffled_multi_column_indices_dataset_level, re-shuffled each epoch
For each page: reads all columns (state, action, image) via read_multi_column_aligned_py in one call
Extracts valid anchor-frame samples from each page, filtering episode boundaries
For edge anchors needing rows from neighboring pages: uses LRU page cache (default 3 pages) to serve cross-page reads without extra disk I/O
Shuffle buffer: when full, pop random sample and yield it; at epoch end, drain buffer in random order

Each yielded sample dict has keys: observation.state (float32, (obs_len, state_dim)), action (float32, (pred_len, action_dim)), observation.images.image (uint8, (obs_len, H, W, 3)), frame_index, episode_index
Comprehensive unit tests for: page iteration, page cache LRU eviction, shuffle buffer fill/drain, episode boundary filtering, single-page sample extraction
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Key design: (1) get_shuffled_multi_column_indices_dataset_level(file_paths, reference_col_idx) returns shuffled (file_idx, rg_idx, page_idx) triples. (2) read_multi_column_aligned_py(file_path, rg_idx, column_indices, page_idx) reads all columns for a page. (3) Page cache is dict keyed by (file_path, rg_idx, page_idx) with LRU eviction. (4) For each page, determine which global rows it contains, then for each row check if it's a valid anchor (obs and pred windows don't cross episode boundaries). (5) Edge anchors: if obs window extends before this page or pred window extends after, read needed rows from page cache (which may trigger a cache miss and disk read of the neighboring page). IMPORTANT: verify read_multi_column_aligned_py handles LIST<FLOAT32> columns — previous PRD found read_multi_column_row_range_py needed Rust fixes for LIST columns. The aligned reader may need the same fix. If so, fix in Rust first. Shuffle buffer memory concern: 10K samples with decoded images could use ~2GB. Consider storing samples with raw PNG bytes in buffer and decoding on yield to reduce memory.

userStories.title: Multi-worker support
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the page-aligned dataset to work with PyTorch DataLoader multi-worker mode, so that data loading can be parallelized across CPU cores.
acceptanceCriteria: In __iter__, check torch.utils.data.get_worker_info() — if multi-worker, partition pages: worker gets pages where page_index % num_workers == worker_id
Supports pickling: __getstate__/__setstate__ exclude ParquetReaderCachePy and page cache, recreate in workers
Each worker maintains its own independent shuffle buffer
Unit test: with 4 workers, verify page partitioning assigns disjoint page sets
Unit test: with 2 workers, verify combined output covers all valid anchors
Integration test: DataLoader with num_workers=4, batch_size=8 produces correct batch shapes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Page partitioning: given N pages and W workers, worker w gets pages at indices w, w+W, w+2W, ... This is simple and balanced. Each worker has its own shuffle buffer and page cache. __getstate__ should exclude _reader_cache, _page_cache, and _shuffle_buffer. __setstate__ recreates _reader_cache via ParquetReaderCachePy().preload(file_paths).

userStories.title: Integration with training loop
userStories.description: As a user running train_qwen_vl_libero.py, I want the page-aligned dataset as the default backend while keeping existing backends available.
acceptanceCriteria: Add youmu_page_aligned as a valid libero_dataset_backend option in build_libero_dataset() in tasks/omni/train_qwen_vl_libero.py
Change default value of libero_dataset_backend from 'youmu' to 'youmu_page_aligned'
DataLoader created with shuffle=False when backend is youmu_page_aligned (shuffling is internal via page shuffle + buffer)
LiberoYoumuPageAlignedDataset provides __len__ returning total valid anchor count for training step calculation
Existing collators work unchanged since each yielded sample matches the standard dict format
Smoke test: 10 training steps with --libero_dataset_backend youmu_page_aligned complete without error
Tests pass
userStories.notes: build_libero_dataset() in tasks/omni/train_qwen_vl_libero.py currently supports youmu, lerobot, lance (default youmu). Add youmu_page_aligned and change default. Key: DataLoader must use shuffle=False for IterableDataset. Check where DataLoader is created and add conditional. HuggingFace Trainer supports IterableDataset but needs __len__ for max_steps calculation — the dataset should compute this from episode metadata (same as LiberoYoumuDataset.anchors count).

userStories.title: Correctness validation
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to verify that the page-aligned dataset produces the exact same set of samples as the row-range dataset, so that training semantics are preserved.
acceptanceCriteria: Test iterates both LiberoYoumuDataset (all indices) and LiberoYoumuPageAlignedDataset (full epoch), collects all (frame_index, episode_index) pairs, verifies the sets are identical
Test that for 100 random anchor frames, tensors (state, action, image) from page-aligned match row-range (torch.allclose for floats, exact match for images)
Test shuffle buffer randomness: first 1000 yielded frame_indices are not in sorted order
Test page cache correctness: edge anchors (first/last valid anchor in a page) produce correct obs/pred windows matching row-range output
Tests pass
userStories.notes: These are integration tests that require the real dataset at /home/ubuntu/dataset/hf_vla_64k. For the full-epoch comparison, iterate LiberoYoumuPageAlignedDataset completely and collect frame_index set. Compare with set(anchor[0] for anchor in LiberoYoumuDataset.anchors). For tensor comparison, create both datasets, pick 100 random frame_indices from the page-aligned output, look up same indices in row-range dataset, and compare tensors.

userStories.title: Unconstrained benchmark
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to benchmark page-aligned against row-range Youmu and LeRobot without memory constraints to establish baseline throughput.
acceptanceCriteria: Add youmu_page_aligned as a valid backend in scripts/benchmark_data_loading.py (create dataset via LiberoYoumuPageAlignedDataset, use iter-based benchmarking for IterableDataset)
Run benchmark with --backends youmu youmu_page_aligned lerobot, standard sweep (num_workers=[0,2,4,8], obs_lens=[1,2,4], batch_sizes=[4,8], iterations=200)
Save results to benchmarks/page_aligned_unconstrained_results.csv
Tests pass
userStories.notes: The benchmark script currently iterates DataLoader via for-loop which works for both map-style and iterable datasets. However, IterableDataset ignores DataLoader's shuffle param — make sure shuffle=False is passed for youmu_page_aligned. Also note: IterableDataset with num_workers>0 means each worker iterates independently, so the effective iteration rate scales with workers. Add create_youmu_page_aligned_dataset() factory function alongside existing create_youmu_dataset().

userStories.title: Memory-constrained benchmark
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to run the cgroup memory-constrained benchmark with all 3 backends to demonstrate page-aligned throughput stability under memory pressure.
acceptanceCriteria: Update scripts/benchmark_memory_sweep.sh to support 3 backends (youmu, youmu_page_aligned, lerobot)
Run sweep across RAM limits [2G, 4G, 8G, 16G, 32G] with all 3 backends
Save results to benchmarks/memory_constrained_page_aligned/
Generate analysis via scripts/analyze_memory_benchmark.py
Results show page-aligned throughput stable across RAM limits while row-range degrades
userStories.notes: The sweep script already supports --backends flag. Just need to ensure benchmark_data_loading.py recognizes youmu_page_aligned. Drop page cache before each backend run (already implemented). Use iterations=50 for reasonable runtime. Skip 1G limit since both youmu backends need ~800MB base.

userStories.title: Write final benchmark report
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a comprehensive report comparing all 3 backends across unconstrained and memory-constrained scenarios.
acceptanceCriteria: Report at benchmarks/page_aligned_benchmark_report.md includes both unconstrained and constrained results
Summary table: throughput (best config) per backend per RAM limit
Analysis: crossover point where page-aligned exceeds LeRobot under memory pressure
Analysis: I/O amplification comparison across backends and RAM limits
Conclusion with recommendation on when to use each backend
userStories.notes: Combine data from US-005 (unconstrained) and US-006 (constrained). Expected findings: unconstrained — page-aligned similar to or slightly better than row-range youmu, LeRobot fastest. Constrained — page-aligned stable, row-range youmu degrades severely, LeRobot degrades moderately. Crossover likely at 4-8G.
